solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unintentionally reveal note about stopping support at the end of May

indicators.note: stopping here means plugging a gap, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: about signals that the note's letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: TE is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: at the end of points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone lets slip a remark about a support being stopped at the end of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unintentionally reveal' is the definition; 'about' turns the note round before 'stopping' places it inside the support, and 'at the end of May' gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something away without meaning to is a common sense of the verb, as when a face betrays fear.

clue.text: Reluctant to support conflict with Germany

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a war is a conflict
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to back a war alongside Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Backward can mean shy or hesitant, as in not being backward in coming forward.

clue.text: Determined canoeist manoeuvred around bend

indicators.note: around tells us the shuffled letters wrap round the bend
manoeuvred suggests the letters of the canoeist being steered into a new order

parts.note: a U-bend is a bend in a pipe, so U stands for bend

explanation.surface: A determined canoeist steers round a bend in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvred' rearranges CANOEIST into TENACIOS, and 'around' places it round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenacious person holds on firmly and will not give up, i.e. is resolute.

clue.text: Clergyman not starting immediately

indicators.note: not starting tells us to drop the first letter of the clergyman word

parts.note: a canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A clergyman who doesn't get going straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an archaic word for soon or at once, as in 'I come anon'.

clue.text: Departs leaving poet with room key

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

indicators.note: leaving says the departing letter is taken away from the poet

parts.note: a bard is a poet
D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: Someone departs, leaving a poet behind along with a room key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departs leaving poet' takes D away from BARD to leave BAR; 'key' is the definition, not a hotel room key.
explanation.definitionFit: The long bar at the bottom of a keyboard is one particular key, used for gaps between words.

clue.text: Alternate in lead with Rosemary for instance

indicators.note: in puts the alternative word inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
alternate as an adjective means other, as in the other one

explanation.surface: An alternate role in a lead part, played with a woman called Rosemary.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosemary looks like a woman's name, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot herb is any herb grown for the kitchen, and rosemary is one example.

clue.text: Girl seen after talk by house mistress some time ago

indicators.note: seen after places the girl's name behind the word for talk

parts.note: to chat is to talk
Elaine is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is spotted after a chat with an old-fashioned housemistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the woman in charge of a large household or castle carried its keys on a chain and ran it.

clue.text: Horse getting up to grab second place in Iraq

indicators.note: to grab means the turned horse takes hold of the second letter
in a down clue getting up means the horse is read bottom to top

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A horse stands up to seize second place in a race in Iraq.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns ARAB into BARA, which grabs S.
explanation.definitionFit: Basra is a major port city in southern Iraq.

clue.text: Quite the artist before onset of rheumatism

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: onset of picks out the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An artist is quite something before rheumatism sets in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning fairly or somewhat, as in rather cold.

clue.text: Caution shown by Tom crossing road

indicators.note: crossing suggests the tomcat spans the road, so the road sits inside it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a road

explanation.surface: A tomcat shows caution while crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a warning or proviso, a Latin word meaning let him beware.

clue.text: In agreement with worker after company takes on new lad

indicators.note: after places the worker behind the company and lad

parts.note: a son is a lad
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A worker agrees after the firm hires a new boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonant with means consistent with or in harmony, a sense taken from music.

clue.text: Like to knit anything useful

parts.note: as means like, as in 'dressed as a clown'
a broken bone is said to knit or set when it heals

explanation.surface: Someone likes knitting, finding anything useful to do.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is any valuable resource or benefit, something of use to its owner.

clue.text: Fictional club not having best fuel supplier

indicators.note: not having tells us to remove the word for best from the club name

parts.note: the Pickwick Club is the fictional club of Dickens's Pickwick Papers
the pick of the bunch is the best

explanation.surface: A fictional club that lacks the best fuel supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pickwick Papers is Dickens's comic novel about Mr Pickwick's club.
explanation.definitionFit: The wick of a candle or lamp draws up the wax or oil that feeds the flame.

clue.text: About to catch erratic teenager in form again

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: erratic means irregular, so the teenager's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is about to catch an unpredictable teenager getting back in form.
explanation.definitionFit: To regenerate is to grow or create anew, as a lizard does with a lost tail.

clue.text: Chap, very old, fast becomes spiteful

parts.note: a chap is a male
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A very old man who goes on a fast and turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm on others, from the Latin for ill-wishing.

clue.text: It was heard by the unruly girl outside Ohio's principal court

definitions.text: It was heard by the unruly

indicators.note: outside puts the girl's name around the leading letter

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

indicators.note: principal means chief, so the first letter of Ohio is taken

explanation.surface: An unruly girl is heard outside Ohio's main court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was read aloud to unruly crowds in Britain, ordering them to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act of 1714 was literally read out to rioters, so it was something those unruly people heard.

clue.text: British boy finally boxing with spirit

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the outer letters surround the word for with
finally picks the last letter of the word boy

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: A British lad finally gets into boxing with real spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport, but here the British abbreviation and the boy's final letter enclose the word for 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine.

clue.text: I'd turned up to collect missing piece of African mask

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters are read upwards
missing says a letter is lost from the word for collect

parts.note: to assemble is to collect or gather

indicators.note: piece of takes just a bit of the word African, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to gather an African mask with a piece missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives DI; ASSEMBLE loses the A from African.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissemble is to hide one's true feelings, to put on a mask.

clue.text: Unpleasantly loud weapons ultimately seen at the front

indicators.note: the final letter of the weapons is shifted to the front of the word

parts.note: tridents are three-pronged spears

explanation.surface: Loud weapons are seen at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of TRIDENTS moves to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is harsh and grating, loud in an unpleasant way.

clue.text: Extremely ambivalent about head backing agreement

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters go round the turned headland
extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters
backing means going backwards, so the headland is read in reverse

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbouring capes

explanation.surface: An extremely ambivalent person nods their head in grudging agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland in British place names; 'backing' turns it round and 'Extremely' supplies the outer letters that go about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is approval or consent, saying yes.

clue.text: Material evidence eventually found by volunteers close to river

parts.note: the Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff in Wales

indicators.note: eventually points to the end, the last letter of evidence

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Material evidence is eventually found by volunteers near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material evidence' looks like a legal phrase; Material alone is the definition. The Taff is a Welsh river; the TA is Britain's army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, smooth fabric, often of silk.

clue.text: Objects to a couple of Etonians with attitude

parts.note: if one minds something one objects to it

indicators.note: a couple of means two, so the first two letters of Etonians are taken

explanation.surface: Someone takes against a couple of Etonians with an attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Etonians are pupils of Eton, the English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a settled way of thinking or outlook.

clue.text: Hands over painting of animal

indicators.note: over means covering, so the hands wrap round the painting

parts.note: hands are workers or crew, i.e. men
painting is a kind of art

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a painting of an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands over' looks like a verb phrase meaning give, but 'Hands' are workers and 'over' means covering the painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A marten is a weasel-like carnivore of forests, such as the pine marten.

clue.text: Seize and execute Lollard leader inside church

indicators.note: inside places the leading letter within the word for execute

parts.note: to execute a stroke is to cut

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Lollard

explanation.surface: Seize and execute the Lollard leader inside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lollards were followers of the medieval heretic John Wycliffe.
explanation.definitionFit: To clutch is to grab hold of tightly.

clue.text: A bullet's flight path produces one if rifle's defective

indicators.note: defective means faulty, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the word rifle as written joins the fodder; the possessive 's adds no letters

explanation.surface: A faulty rifle sends a bullet off course.
explanation.definitionFit: The line of fire is the direct path along which a gun's shot travels.

clue.text: Loaded fellow's catch onto buggy at first

parts.note: to nab is to catch

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A rich man's catch is loaded onto a buggy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a very wealthy person, originally one rich from India.

clue.text: Even island folk regard it as a creature of legend

parts.note: yet means even, as in yet more

explanation.surface: Even islanders consider it a mythical creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the abominable snowman said to roam the Himalayas.

clue.text: Cease to associate with doctor at work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone stops mixing with a doctor at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a friend is to stop seeing them.

clue.text: Put forward for discussion by panel

definitions.meaning: in British use, to ... a motion is to propose it for debate

explanation.surface: A motion is proposed for a committee to debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabling a motion submits it to a meeting; a table is also a flat panel or slab.

clue.text: European politician keeping essentially perky after former partner becomes hateful

indicators.note: after puts the European and politician behind the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the politician holds the central letter

parts.note: Vince Cable is a British Liberal Democrat politician

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, the middle letter of perky

explanation.surface: A European politician, keeping cheerful after a former partner, turns hateful.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable was a British Liberal Democrat leader and minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means utterly detestable, deserving to be cursed.

clue.text: Customary for a prince to consume a fairly large amount you say

indicators.note: to consume means to take in, so the prince swallows the rest

parts.note: Hal is Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare
quite a bit is a fair amount, so a bit here

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken and replaced by the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: you said out loud is the letter U

explanation.surface: It's customary for a prince to eat quite a lot, you might say.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual means done by habit, regular and usual.

clue.text: Optimistic over going on strike

parts.note: up means over or finished, as in time's up
to beat is to strike

explanation.surface: Cheerful about going on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means cheerful and positive.
